title: bug: a recycled PID wedges the Claude launch lock forever, and the daemon lane reaps a possibly-live holder's lock unconditionally
description:
MEASURED on this host 2026-09-08T22:1xZ by worker-812079a7 + worker-bcaa6d5e (no row held; reported, not remediated). Topical home is epic-bd387eeb (task-4a3b5ec0 built this lock); filed here because this is the live bug epic.

REPRO/EVIDENCE (1): tmpdir()/moe-claude-launch-locks/212fff9b8089...lock records holder PID 44088, mtimeMs 1788154346969 = 2026-08-31T05:32:26.969Z. `Get-Process 44088` = ALIVE, node, StartTime 2026-09-05T20:39:20.786Z — the lock was written 5d15h BEFORE the process now holding that number started, so the record is a recycled PID. pidIsDead (claude-launch-lock.ts:34) uses process.kill(pid,0), which only answers "a process with this number exists", so it returns false, the attempt===0 reclaim branch at :84 never fires, reapStaleLaunchLock is never reached, and the caller gets a plain LAUNCH_LOCK_IDENTITY_CONFLICT — indistinguishable from legitimate contention. The module header calls this "delays reclaim"; it is UNBOUNDED for as long as the recycled number belongs to a long-lived process. Mutual exclusion is NOT broken; liveness is.

REPRO/EVIDENCE (2): apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts:211-222 afterEach rmSync's sha256("lock-1") UNCONDITIONALLY, no liveness check, after every case. Production lockIdentity is never a literal (per-claim field, foundation-attempt-store.ts:35), so this only collides when a LIVE lane runs fixture-shaped claims — i.e. a foundation e2e arm, the arm most likely running when it matters. That path reaps a live holder's lock by name.

SEVERITY SPLIT: test identities are `<prefix>${process.pid}-${Date.now()}`, so a wedged residue identity can never be re-requested (harmless disk residue — 2 of the 4 files on this host record 40000000, the exact seed of firstDeadPid() at claude-launcher.test.ts:61). "lock-1" is FIXED, hence requestable forever: a wedge there halts that lane permanently.

FIX DIRECTION (agreed after one rejected proposal): do NOT use a wall-clock staleness bound — worker-812079a7 proposed it and withdrew it; the heartbeat lapses in exactly the conditions that make a launch slow (usage-limit pause, -Interactive idle seat, suspend/resume, blocked loop) and an NTP step ages a fresh lock past any bound. A holder-side re-run of the existing ino/dev binding check does not rescue it (check-then-act, window = the whole 63-216s launch; a stalled holder cannot re-check while stalled). Correct fix: open the lock WITHOUT FILE_SHARE_DELETE (share mode 0x3, not 0x7) so the reap's rename — already the sole arbitration point, reapStaleLaunchLock:64 — fails ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION while the holder's handle is open and succeeds the instant the holder is gone, however it died. Kernel-enforced mutual exclusion, crash-reclaim with no probe, no PID load-bearing, no time bound. fs.open always passes 0x7; repo precedent for reaching past it is tools/packaging/pack-windows-publication-source.ts:27-45 (SHARE_* + ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION) and pack-windows-candidate.test.ts:33 (CreateFileW(path,0x40000000,0x7,...)). No portability cost: claude-launcher.ts:139-140 already refuses non-win32.

Acquire: `net.createServer((s) => { s.on("error", () => {}); s.destroy(); })` then `listen(pipeName)`. That connection handler is ACCEPT-AND-DROP and it is mandatory in exactly that shape: a server with no handler still accepts and RETAINS a libuv pipe handle per connect (71 after 200 connects, measured, versus 1 for accept-and-drop), and a handler that WRITES an identity banner kills the holder — a rival that times out and destroys its socket makes the holder's later `sock.end` throw an unhandled EPIPE, exit 1, mid-launch (measured cross-process). DELETE `recordedHolderPid`, `pidIsDead` and `reapStaleLaunchLock` and the whole attempt/retry loop — they are the defect, not machinery to preserve. Say instead what the ruling comment says: the disease was never that a file existed, it was that the file was LOAD-BEARING FOR MUTUAL EXCLUSION, which let a recycled PID impersonate its holder. Keep the file under 250 physical lines.

   false return becomes `CLAUDE_LAUNCH_LOCK_UNKNOWN` at `:321-323`.
   `new Promise(res => server.close(res))` passes; a thenable or hand-rolled
   wrapper reports an unproven release on a release that actually succeeded.
   Silent if got wrong.

3) THE REGRESSION THE SWAP INTRODUCES IS ATTRIBUTION, NOT THE ACL. Today a stuck
   lock is a FILE with a PID in it — that is the only reason the `44088`
   PID-reuse wedge was diagnosable. A wedged pipe answers `EADDRINUSE` and
   nothing else: no PID, no mtime, no bytes, no reap. Squatter, orphaned seat and
   stalled fleet process are indistinguishable. The swap is strictly better on
   residue and strictly WORSE on diagnosis; the row should buy the diagnosis back.

4) HOW TO BUY IT BACK — and the naive way is a remote-crash primitive.
   A holder that serves an identity BANNER on connection kills itself when a
   rival times out and destroys the socket. Reproduced cross-process (holder in
   parent, rival a real child, holder loop spun 2500ms):
